subtitle: Variant 11 • 45 tasks • 55 scored items • 3 hours • with formula sheet and calculator

cards.title: Quantum and Nuclear Physics
formulas: Conservation laws for A and Z

questions.text: Using the graph, determine the distance travelled by the body in the time interval from 2 s to 5 s. (m)

The body moves with uniform acceleration. Its initial speed is 10 m/s and its speed at the end of the path is 30 m/s. Determine the speed of the body when it has covered half of the path. (m/s)  √5 ≈ 2.24
Two mutually perpendicular forces F₁ = 15 N and F₂ = 20 N act on a body of mass 5 kg. Determine the acceleration of the body. (m/s²)
As shown in the figure, a body slides down an inclined plane with an angle of 37°. The coefficient of friction is μ = 0.25, g = 10 m/s². Determine the acceleration of the body along the plane. (m/s²)

The three bodies shown in the figure move along a surface. The coefficient of friction is the same for all bodies, μ = 0.2. If the system moves under a force F = 60 N, determine the tensions T₁ and T₂ in the strings. (N)
A body is thrown vertically upward and returns to the launch point after 6 s. Determine the maximum height reached by the body. (m)
A body sinks in kerosene with an acceleration of 4 m/s². With what acceleration will this body sink in water? ρ_water = 1 g/cm³, ρ_kerosene = 0.8 g/cm³, g = 10 m/s².

In the system shown in the figure, a force F = 20 N directed to the right acts on block m₂. The coefficient of friction on all surfaces is μ = 0.2, and the spring constant is k = 200 N/m. If the system moves at constant velocity, what is the extension of the spring? (cm)
A simple pendulum is placed in an elevator cabin moving downward with an acceleration of 0.36g. By what percentage does its period of oscillation increase?

When an ideal gas passes from state 1 to state 2, its pressure does not change while its volume increases by a factor of 2. If the temperature changed by 300 K, find the initial temperature of the gas. (K)
The density of an ideal gas is 1.2 kg/m³ and its pressure is 16 kPa. Determine the root-mean-square speed of the gas molecules. (m/s)
A load of mass 4 kg with a base area of 20 cm² stands on the floor of an elevator accelerating upward at 2 m/s². Find the pressure exerted by the load on the floor. (Pa)
How much heat is released when 3 liters of water at 0 °C freeze completely? λ = 334 kJ/kg. (kJ)
To what height will water rise in a capillary tube of diameter 0.2 mm? The water wets the tube completely. σ = 73 mN/m, ρ = 1000 kg/m³, g = 10 m/s². (cm)
In the circuit segment shown in the figure, the current flows from point A to point B. If R = 4 Ω and I = 3 A, determine φA − φB. (V)

Capacitors C₁ = 4 nF and C₂ = 2 nF are connected in parallel, and a capacitor C₃ = 3 nF is connected in series with this combination. If the charge of the first capacitor is 8 nC, find the charge of the third capacitor. (nC)

After the external circuit is connected, the voltage across the battery terminals is 18 V. The external resistance is R = 6 Ω and the battery EMF is ε = 24 V. Find the internal resistance of the battery. (Ω)

In three identical conductors connected in parallel to a power supply, a certain amount of heat is released in t₁ = 40 s. How much time is needed to release the same amount of heat if these conductors are connected in series?

In the circuit shown in the figure, the 40 Ω and 10 Ω resistors are connected in parallel. The EMF of the source is 10 V and the current in the main circuit is 1 A. Determine the short-circuit current of the source. (A)
What kinetic energy does a charge of 2 μC acquire after passing, from rest, through a potential difference of 500 V? (mJ)
20 identical capacitors are connected in parallel. The capacitance of each capacitor is 4 μF. If 10 J of heat was released while charging the battery, determine the voltage across the capacitors. (V)
A capacitor of capacitance 1 μF is connected to an alternating-current circuit of frequency 50 Hz. Determine its capacitive reactance.
A force F = 0.15 N acts on a conductor of length l = 0.5 m placed perpendicular to a magnetic field of induction B = 2·10⁻² T. Find the current in the conductor. (A)
A resistance of 40 Ω is connected to an alternating-current circuit. The RMS value of the current is 5 A. Determine the maximum value of the voltage. (V)
When the string of a simple pendulum is shortened by 5 cm, its frequency increases by a factor of 1.5. Find the initial length of the pendulum string. (cm)

The primary winding of a step-down transformer with a transformation ratio of 8 is connected to a 220 V supply. The resistance of the secondary winding is 2 Ω and the current in it is 3 A. Find the voltage across the terminals of the secondary winding. (V)

A lens with a focal length of 10 cm produces a real image of an object reduced by a factor of 2. Another lens, with the object in the same position, produced a real image magnified by a factor of 2. Find the focal length of the second lens. (cm)
An object is at a distance of 5F from a converging lens. By what factor is the resulting image smaller than the object?
The energy of photons incident on a metal is 7.8·10⁻¹⁹ J and the work function of the metal is 3.0·10⁻¹⁹ J. Determine the stopping voltage for the photoelectrons. (V)
The work function of the metal is 6·10⁻¹⁹ J and the maximum kinetic energy of the photoelectrons is 6·10⁻²⁰ J. Find the wavelength of the incident light. h = 6.6·10⁻³⁴ J·s, c = 3·10⁸ m/s. (nm)
If the momentum of a photon is 1.1·10⁻²⁷ kg·m/s, determine the wavelength of this light. h = 6.6·10⁻³⁴ J·s. (nm)
Identify the unknown particle X in the following nuclear reaction: X + ¹²₆C → ⁴₂He + ¹₀n + ¹⁶₈O
During the 2 → 3 transition, 60 kJ of heat is supplied to the gas. By how much did the internal energy of the gas change? (kJ)

questions.text: A body falls freely from a height of 180 m. g = 10 m/s².

parts.text: Determine the time it takes the body to reach the ground.
Determine the speed of the body 3 s after it is released.

questions.text: A body of mass 2 kg is suspended from a spring with a spring constant of 400 N/m.

parts.text: Find the extension of the spring if the elevator moves upward with an acceleration of 5 m/s².
Find the extension of the spring if the elevator moves downward at a constant speed of 5 m/s.

questions.text: The two bodies shown in the figure rest on a horizontal surface. For all surfaces μ = 0.2, g = 10 m/s².

parts.text: Determine the acceleration of the system.
Find the tension in the string connecting the bodies.

questions.text: Two bodies of mass 5 kg each move in the same direction with speeds of 3 m/s and 5 m/s, respectively. The bodies collide inelastically and move together.

parts.text: Determine the common speed after the collision.
Find the kinetic energy of the system after the collision.

questions.text: A monatomic ideal gas receives 10 kJ of heat in an isobaric process.

parts.text: Determine the change in the internal energy of the gas.
Determine the work done on the gas by external forces.

questions.text: In the figure, a resistor of resistance 11 Ω is connected to a source with an EMF of 26 V. A current of 2 A flows through the resistor.

parts.text: Determine the internal resistance of the source.
Determine the short-circuit current of the source.

questions.text: In a series circuit, R = 5 Ω, Xₗ = 20 Ω, X꜀ = 8 Ω.

parts.text: Find the total impedance.
What is the total impedance if the resistance is zero?

questions.text: In a converging lens with a focal length F = 6 cm, a real image of the source is formed at a distance of 12 cm from the lens.

parts.text: Determine the magnification of the lens.
Find the distance between the object and the lens.

questions.text: A converging lens with a focal length F = 10 cm and an object of height h = 2 cm are given.

parts.text: Determine the height of the real image when the object is 5 cm beyond the focal point.
Determine the height of the virtual image when the object is 5 cm inside the focal point.

questions.text: The intensity of light incident on a surface is 9 kW/m².

parts.text: Determine the light pressure when the surface reflects the light completely.
Determine the light pressure when the surface absorbs the light completely.
